display_title: [XLA][BufferAssignment] Cache fixed-offset state on BufferAllocation

head_commit.message:
[XLA][BufferAssignment] Cache fixed-offset state on BufferAllocation

Previously, `BufferAssigner::MaybeAssignBuffer` and
`BufferAssignment::CombineTempAllocations` iterated over
`allocation->assigned_buffers()` (`absl::flat_hash_map`) on every candidate
buffer to check whether an allocation already contained fixed-offset buffers or
buffers at a different offset. Furthermore, `MaybeAssignBuffer` performed this
check after the `LiveRangeInterferes` loop, paying for `buffer_live_ranges`
hash lookups even on allocations incompatible with the candidate's fixed-offset
requirements.

This change:
1. Caches `has_zero_fixed_offset_buffer_`, `has_nonzero_fixed_offset_buffer_`,
   `all_buffers_at_same_offset_`, and `common_offset_` directly on
   `BufferAllocation`.
2. Hoists the O(1) fixed-offset compatibility check in `MaybeAssignBuffer`
   ahead of `cached_new_live_ranges` and the `LiveRangeInterferes` loop,
   eliminating both `allocation->assigned_buffers()` scans and short-circuiting
   live-range interference checks on incompatible allocations.
3. Replaces the `assigned_buffers()` scans in `CombineTempAllocations` with O(1)
   queries on `BufferAllocation` and removes the now-unused
   `fixed_offset_for_value` parameter.
4. Adds unit tests verifying fixed-offset allocation reuse and rejection of
   non-fixed buffers on fixed-offset allocations.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 995912677

display_title: [XLA][BufferAssignment] Precompute required fixed offsets per buffer

head_commit.message:
[XLA][BufferAssignment] Precompute required fixed offsets per buffer

Previously, `BufferAssigner` repeatedly invoked `opts_.fixed_offset` across
`hlo_buffer.values()` and `allocation->assigned_buffers()` inside
`MaybeAssignBuffer`, `DelayTemporaryBufferAssignment`, `AssignSingleHloBuffer`,
and `BufferAssignment::CombineTempAllocations`. On modules with many buffers
participating in fixed-offset buffer assignment, this resulted in quadratic
callback evaluations and `HloAliasAnalysis::GetUniqueBufferAt` lookups.

This change:
1. Precomputes dense `fixed_offset_for_buffer_` (indexed by `HloBuffer::Id`)
   and `fixed_offset_for_value_` (indexed by `HloValue::Id`) vectors once in
   `BufferAssigner::PrecomputeFixedOffsets` immediately after buffer coloring
   in `BufferAssigner::CreateAssignment`, validating conflicting or negative
   fixed offsets upfront.
2. Replaces all repeated `opts_.fixed_offset` callback loops in
   `MaybeAssignBuffer`, `DelayTemporaryBufferAssignment`,
   `AssignSingleHloBuffer`, and `CombineTempAllocations` with O(1) lookups into
   the precomputed tables.
3. Adds unit tests verifying that `opts.fixed_offset` is evaluated once per
   `HloValue` and that conflicting fixed offsets on aliased values return an
   error.

display_title: [Mosaic] Replace and erase original op before running downgrade rules in RunSerde.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic] Replace and erase original op before running downgrade rules in RunSerde.

Previously, `RunSerde` passed `new_op` to `downgrade_rules` before replacing uses of `op` with `new_op` and erasing `op`. As a result, `new_op` had no uses during the downgrade rule (preventing downgrade rules from inserting post-processing ops that consume `new_op`), and setting `was_erased = true` in a downgrade rule would leave the unmangled `op` behind.

Replace `op`'s uses with `new_op` and erase `op` before invoking `downgrade_rules`, and split `SerdeRuleType` into `UpgradeRuleType` and `DowngradeRuleType` (removing the unused `bool&` parameter from downgrade rules). Bump `JAX_IFRT_VERSION_NUMBER` to 82 so that Mosaic GPU picks the matching rule types.

Keep `SerdeRuleType` and a `RunSerde` overload that takes `SerdeRuleType` downgrade rules as deprecated aliases, so that JAX versions that predate this change still build.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Propagate tile constraints in XTile indexing emission to elide bounds masks.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Propagate tile constraints in XTile indexing emission to elide bounds masks.

When tiling `concatenate` regions in XTile, `SymbolicTileAnalysis` records branch-specific range constraints on each operand `Tile` (such as `offset in [0, N)` inside its active `scf.if` branch), but `EvaluateTilingParameters` previously ignored `TiledHloInstruction::tile().constraints()` when constructing the `IndexingMap` for `xla.apply_indexing`. As a result, `IsGuaranteedInBounds` evaluated the unconstrained `IndexingMap` domain across all `concatenate` branches—which can include negative offsets or offsets exceeding an individual operand's dimension—forcing unnecessary per-element bounds masks (`arith.cmpi` + `arith.andi`) on tile-aligned `concatenate` operand loads.

Add `tile_constraints` to `offset_indexing_map` and call `offset_indexing_map.Simplify()` in `EvaluateTilingParameters`, preserving narrowed `xla.range` annotations when a constrained offset simplifies to a bare variable (and teaching `ApplyIndexingOp` folding and `XTileEntryToTriton` to retain tighter `xla.range` bounds). Guard out-of-range tiles in `EmitConcatenate` when the concatenate dimension offset is not provably within `[0, concat_dim_size)` (such as under surrounding `pad`), and use `xla::GetRange` with overflow-safe feasibility checks in `IsGuaranteedInBounds` and `TritonXlaCollapseContiguousMinorDimsPass`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add layout-aware CudnnScaledDotRewriter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add layout-aware CudnnScaledDotRewriter.

Add a pass that rewrites kScaledDot with K-minor physical layouts into
__cudnn$fusion, with inline scale padding and swizzling. The pass gives
kScaledDot the same flow as kDot: a library rewrite of unfused ops after
GemmFusion, instead of an in-place change of __triton_gemm in the autotuner.
It also lets the autotuner compare Triton and cuDNN through fission.
A later change wires it after GemmFusion and into the autotuner.

The pass pads the scales only along the contracting dimension, so the fused
scaled dot needs no slices. It skips M or N that is not a multiple of 128,
and shapes that cuDNN rejects: K that is not 16-byte aligned, and MXFP4 with

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Account for tile stride in Triton pointer-lowering bounds check.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Account for tile stride in Triton pointer-lowering bounds check.

`IsGuaranteedInBounds` checked `offset + size <= shape`, i.e. it assumed the
tile covers `size` contiguous elements. For strided tiles the last element is
at `offset + (size - 1) * stride`, so e.g. a 4-element tile with stride 4 at
offset 0 in a dimension of size 12 touches index 12, one past the end. Because
the offset is divisible by the tile size and the shape is divisible too, the
mask was skipped entirely and the load/store went out of bounds.

The check now uses the actual extent of the tile (also handling negative
strides), so such tiles get a bounds mask.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Don't use AMD TDM for tiles with out-of-bounds singleton offsets.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Decline AMD TDM for tiles with out-of-bounds singleton offsets.

Tile propagation through `pad` can produce tile offsets that point past the end
of a dimension, e.g. `pid mod 16` for a dimension of size 4 for tiles that lie
entirely in the high padding (b/568080363). Lowerings must therefore never
access memory outside the buffer, whatever the offsets are.

The AMD TDM lowering folds the offsets of singleton (size-1) tile dims into the
base pointer and drops those dims from the tensor descriptor, so they escape
the hardware bounds check. For example, a `[1, 64]` tile of `memref<4x64>` at
offset `[5, 0]` would read elements 320..383 of a 256-element buffer. TDM is now
declined unless those offsets are provably in bounds, falling back to the
masked pointer lowering.

Also documents the out-of-bounds semantics of `xtile.extract` and
`xtile.insert`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Lower ApproxTopK fallback to unstable sort on CPU and GPU.

head_commit.message:
Lower ApproxTopK fallback to unstable sort on CPU and GPU.

`ApproxTopK` on TPU already aggregates candidates using an unstable sort (`is_stable=false`), whereas `ApproxTopKFallback` on CPU and GPU previously forced `is_stable=true`. On XLA:GPU, requiring stability routed `approx_top_k` through a 64-bit key/index bit-packing adapter rather than dispatching directly to the native unstable `select_k` kernel.

`is_stable=true` was set in July 2026 as a workaround because lowering `approx_top_k` with `is_stable=false` exposed an XLA:GPU layout assignment bug where non-default operand layouts (such as `{0, 1}` propagated from an upstream `all-gather`) were passed into `__gpu$TopK` and the RAFT `select_k` kernel, which require contiguous default (`{1, 0}`) input layout. Now that `GpuLayoutAssignment` explicitly constrains `__gpu$TopK` operands to default layout, `approx_top_k` can safely lower with `is_stable=false`.

Switch `ApproxTopKFallback` to emit `is_stable=false`, aligning CPU and GPU semantics with TPU and allowing XLA:GPU to dispatch `approx_top_k` directly to RAFT `select_k` without U64 packing and unpacking overhead.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1009779677

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU][NFC] Deduplicate multi-term emulation in DotAlgorithmRewriter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU][NFC] Deduplicate multi-term emulation in DotAlgorithmRewriter.

Extract shared helpers in `xla/backends/gpu/transforms/dot_algorithm_rewriter.cc` to eliminate repeated operand-splitting and partial-product accumulation code across `RewriteF32ToBF16X3`, `RewriteF32ToBF16X6`, `RewriteF32ToBF16X9`, `RewriteF32ToTF32X3`, and the corresponding `MakeMultiplyFor*` methods:
- `Split2xToBF16OperandPairs`, `Split2xToTF32OperandPairs`, and `Split3xToBF16OperandPairs` split `lhs` and `rhs` and return the ordered `(lhs_part, rhs_part)` operand pairs (`X6` takes the last 6 of the 9 3-way split pairs).
- `AccumulatePartialProducts` sums the lower-order terms left-to-right, zeroes out `NaN`s via `ReplaceNaNWithZeros`, and adds the highest-order term.
- `RewriteDotWithOperandPairs` and `MakeMultiplyWithOperandPairs` build the partial dots (`HloOpcode::kAdd` on `F32` dot outputs) or elementwise products (`Mult` and `SumToF32`) and accumulate them via `AccumulatePartialProducts`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1009719398
